answer_1.quote: We train models for CQA to focus on regions where humans typically fixate, thereby improving both alignment and interpretability. As shown in Figure..., models trained with our approach produce more interpretable and human-aligned attention maps, leading to more accurate answers.

answer_2.quote: Since our dataset consists of yes/no questions, we use accuracy, defined as the percentage of questions correctly answered, to compare chart understanding performance across different models. To assess the similarity between the LVLM attention maps and the human attention maps, we used three standard metrics commonly used in saliency prediction: Pearson's Correlation Coefficient (CC), Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, and histogram intersection (SIM).
